We are looking for software engineering interns for our Sparse Linear Algebra team, which develops libraries like cuSPARSE that are a key part of high-performance computing and deep learning software stacks. The main purpose of these libraries is to provide the fastest computing primitives for operations like sparse matrix-vector and sparse matrix-matrix products, among many others. We see strong interest in optimization of such key functionalities from various industrial and research organizations - from gaming and machine learning to autonomous driving and chip modeling. All of these operations need to be optimized for current and future GPUs and for a wide range of unstructured sparse matrix inputs, which can also necessitate changing the underlying algorithms mathematically and using techniques like code/kernel generation. Does the idea of being at the heart of these projects and applying your knowledge to develop and optimize algorithms which make an impact around world excite you? If yes, then come and join our team!

During your internship, you will work with senior software engineers on the libraries team who will provide mentorship and guide you in developing highly optimized algorithms. Projects will involve implementing new numerical algorithms, defining APIs, analyzing performance, finding appropriate solutions for difficult numerical corner cases, and other general software engineering work.

What you'll be doing:

• Prototype and develop numerical algorithms for high-performance sparse linear algebra libraries for GPUs

• Analyze the performance of GPU implementations and find opportunities for improvements

• Collaborate with team members to understand software use cases and requirements

What we need to see:

• Pursuing MS or PhD in Computational Science, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or equivalent program area.

• Strong C++ programming, debugging, performance analysis, and test design skills

• Experience implementing sparse linear algebra algorithms

• Parallel programming experience using CUDA and/or OpenMP

• Experience with domain-specific language design, code/kernel generation, and compiler optimizations

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Exposure to numerical methods, floating-point arithmetic and numerical error analysis

• Knowledge of GPU/CPU and network hardware architecture

• A scripting language, preferably Python

• Understanding of composability and fusions, compilers, and implementation of programming languages

• Familiarity with recent CUDA developments like cuTILE and Tile++ and eExperience with sparse compilers (MLIR or TACO)

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you!

Do you enjoy hacking and tinkering at the lowest levels of software? Are you capable of crafting and implementing creative secure firmware solutions in heavily resource-constrained environments? If so, you’re primed to help develop the boot software that powers the world’s best GPUs.  NVIDIA is searching for an outstanding security software engineer to fill an exciting, yet fun role on our GPU Firmware team. You will be joining a team whose primary mission is solving the intricate enigma of securing and innovating the boot process for our GPUs, while working through the formidable constraints of boot-time and storage space. Every. Byte. Counts.

The GPU Firmware team builds the root of trust firmware for GPUs that provides secure boot, update, and attestation services for all our GPU products from gaming to high-performance compute in the datacenter. • Work within a larger virtual security team on other parts of the GPU stack, as necessary

What we need to see:

• BS or MS degree in EE/CS/CE (or equivalent experience)

• 5+ years’ experience in developing device BIOS, firmware, or other low-level software

• 2+ years’ experience in building secure firmware and working with hardware security components

• Strong C skills

• Secure software fundamentals including cryptography, authentication/attestation, chains of trust, and understanding of common SW security vulnerabilities

• Easy to work with, as you’ll constantly work closely with both hardware designers and other software engineers to design, develop, and debug functional (and non-functional!) aspects of GPU subsystems

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Experience with threat modeling, formal design analysis, hardware/firmware architecture, and other demonstrable security experience in a defensive security focused role.

• Build scalable, reproducible infrastructure for training experiments, evaluation pipelines, and model performance analysis.

• Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) in Computer Science or AI with 12+ years of meaningful work experience.

• Excellent programming skills in Python and strong understanding of large language models, transformer architectures, and the training and evaluation of generative models.

• Foundational understanding of reinforcement learning algorithms and implementation, including MDPs, policies, and reward design.

• Deep understanding of software engineering fundamentals, code generation, automated testing, and program correctness.

• Proven track record to lead model development life cycles, including dataset versioning, experiment tracking, and evaluation pipelines.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Experience training or post-training state-of-the-art coding models or models designed for software engineering agents.

• Experience with execution-based rewards, verifiable rewards, reward hacking mitigation, and automated code evaluation.

We are looking for a senior networking engineer to lead the network architecture of our GPU superclusters. Own and evolve the Kubernetes networking architecture for GPU clusters running at multi-thousand-node scale

Find and eliminate scale ceilings: packet loss under load, control-plane saturation, IP address management exhaustion, and the failure modes that only appear above a few thousand nodes

Build the scale-test environments and validation suites that let us catch networking regressions before they reach production, rather than during a training run

Diagnose hard, ambiguous problems across the stack - where a symptom in Slurm or a training job traces back to a mark collision, a stale route, or a saturated tunnel

Autonomous agents now do real work across NVIDIA, and every piece underneath them keeps changing: models, harnesses, tools, skills, and plugins. Evaluation is how a team knows whether a change made an agent better or quietly made it worse. We're looking for a principal engineer to set evaluation strategy at every layer, from individual skills and MCP servers to whole agents and products, and to design how agents use those results to improve themselves.

Agents can already rewrite the skills and plugins they run on, then test whether the change helped. Making that loop trustworthy is the hard part. What does it take for an agent to get better on its own, and prove the improvement is real? We're building a system that answers that question for every agent at NVIDIA. Come build it with us!

What you'll be doing:

• Build evaluation that works the same across harnesses, with automated checks on every change that catch regressions before users do.

• Mine production traces for failures, new usage patterns, missing skills and tools, cost and latency hot spots, and successful runs. Turn them into eval cases and improvement signals.

• Evaluate the eval datasets themselves: coverage of real usage, duplicate cases, and how closely they match production.

• Build the self-improvement loop for evolving harnesses: agents propose changes to their own skills, plugins, and harness configuration, and sandboxed evals test each one. Only measurable gains ship, with human sign-off and limits agents can't change.

• Create realistic enterprise environments: sandboxed replicas of issue trackers, code repositories, chat, and internal APIs, filled with synthetic or anonymized data, where agents safely run long, end-to-end tasks.

• Measure multi-agent swarms as a team: how agents split work, whether handoffs succeed, and whether permissions hold at every hop. Record how long each task takes and how many tokens it uses.

• Keep evals honest: calibrate model and agent judges against human labels. Catch agents that cheat, such as working backward from expected answers or reaching data and tools they shouldn't access. We work closely with product, platform, and hardware teams throughout NVIDIA, and we help shape open evaluation standards and benchmarks across the industry.

What we need to see:

• BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience)

• 12+ years building large-scale systems, including evaluation systems for ML or agents and the data pipelines that feed them

• Hands-on experience building and evaluating agents on an open or closed agent harness

• Solid grounding in experiment design: statistical significance, variance across repeated runs, and A/B testing

• Experience setting technical direction across teams as a senior individual contributor

• Proficiency in Python, Go, Rust, or similar

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Built self-improving or self-evolving agent systems that get better from their own eval results

• Shipped an agent benchmark, eval framework, or simulated test environment adopted by other teams

• Detected reward hacking or eval gaming, or built oversight for systems that modify themselves

• Built domain evaluations, such as for chip design or hardware verification

We are searching for a Senior Compiler Engineer in our GPU Software organization. We deliver features and improvements that help NVIDIA hardware reach its full potential across a growing range of computational workloads, from deep learning and scientific computing to self-driving cars, video games, and virtual reality. Our compiler organization makes its mark on every GPU NVIDIA produces.

The CUDA programming language defines a unified programming model across a range of system configurations and hardware capabilities. The compiler translates parallel programs written in higher-level languages, like CUDA C++, into microcode optimized for fast execution on NVIDIA’s family of industry-leading GPU architectures. More and more of that code is now written with the help of AI agents, and the compiler front end is where developers and agents first meet the language. In this role, you will focus on the CUDA compiler front end, building language features, diagnostics, and capabilities that help both developers and agents write correct, high-performance GPU code. You’ll also have the opportunity to grow into other parts of the compiler stack, including the LLVM-based optimizer, code generation, and MLIR.

Securing NVIDIA's EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying a standard security stack. The workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for an off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. You'll be an individual contributor on Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters, the team that implements security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA's hardware engineers design silicon on - spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud. You will sit alongside the engineers who run these clusters 24x7, close enough to deploy a control, investigate a behavior, and change the running environment yourself.

This is hands-on build work, not control review. You'll decide where conventional tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and then engineer the alternative. If your depth is in large-scale compute, networking, or storage infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job, and you've carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you're who we want to talk to. We don't expect fluency in every security product category. We expect you to own outcomes and pick up the remaining domain breadth fast. Security engineering here is engineering: code, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure - not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets.

What You'll Be Doing:

• Build and operate security controls and telemetry for EDA compute, storage, and networking - design, ship to production, then own them.

• Engineer around hard constraints. Protect multi-day, high-value compute jobs without degrading them. Where heavyweight in-node agents are not viable, build the workable answer instead.

• Make the network and platform the control plane. Protection can't depend solely on what runs inside the node.

• Instrument for detection. Collect and normalize security signals from the fleet into our SIEM, and build the detections and dashboards that turn it into something actionable. Log collection alone is not monitoring.

• Investigate and respond. Chase down EDA-specific threats and exposure, and execute containment and remediation hands-on with infrastructure and service owners.

• Automate enforcement and evidence. Infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state, with compliance evidence produced as an engineering output rather than a manual exercise.

• Run the lifecycle of the security technologies you own: selection, rollout, operation, and eventual replacement.

• Work across boundaries. Partner directly with data center operations, IT storage and networking, network engineering, CSP teams, and NVIDIA's central security organization on shared outcomes.

• Think like an adversary. Threat modeling and mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute.

What We Need To See:

• 8+ years of hands-on infrastructure or infrastructure-security engineering across on-prem and cloud environments.

• Strong Linux depth - you are comfortable at the system level, not just the console level.

• Real experience operating or securing compute fleets at scale: provisioning, lifecycle, and the operational realities of long-running jobs.

• Working networking expertise applied to large compute environments.

• Programming/scripting fluency (Python, Go, or shell) used for automation, detection, and tooling you've shipped and maintained.

• Solid foundations in access control, authentication, segmentation, encryption, and vulnerability lifecycle.

• A track record of landing changes with partners who don't report to you.

• Clear written and verbal communication - credible with individual engineers and with leadership.

• A Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering field or equivalent experience.

Ways To Stand Out from the Crowd:

• Security or platform engineering inside EDA, HPC, or large research-cluster environments.

• Breadth across security domains - IAM, EDR/XDR, CNAPP, CSPM, zero-trust architectures - or a demonstrated pattern of picking up new domains fast.

• Built or operated infrastructure security capabilities at a hyperscaler or a security product company - you engineered detection and enforcement systems rather than deploying someone else's.

• Contributions to open-source security or infrastructure tooling.

The AI revolution is not powered by models alone, rather it advances when enormous amounts of computation become fast, efficient, and economical enough to turn new ideas into products people can use on a global scale. Faster training lets research and product teams test the next idea sooner. Lower-latency, higher-throughput inference makes AI assistants and agents more responsive and practical for more people. Shorter time to solution lets scientists and engineers explore more possibilities within the same time and energy budget.

At NVIDIA, performance is not a supporting metric — it is how architectural invention becomes useful computing. CUDA is a critical layer where that transformation happens, sitting beneath the frameworks, libraries, and applications used across AI, deep learning, and HPC, as well as graphics, automotive, robotics, and other CUDA-powered products. That gives this team unusual leverage: reduce overhead in a fundamental launch, synchronization, memory, or data-movement path—or create a new driver or runtime capability—and the improvement can flow through many downstream systems and be repeated across vast numbers of products. One well-designed systems feature can help customers obtain more useful work from GPUs already deployed while informing how future CUDA capabilities and GPU architectures are designed.

We are looking for systems software engineers who want to work at this leverage point. You will design and ship production C/C++ features and optimizations in the CUDA driver and runtime, trace important workloads across application, operating-system, CPU, interconnect, and GPU boundaries, bring up new platforms, and turn evidence into future software and hardware direction. Your work will not end at a benchmark: it can make AI tools more responsive and efficient, help scientists reach answers sooner, and enable intelligent machines and interactive products to operate within demanding real-time constraints. Over time, you can grow from owning critical features and performance paths to setting subsystem direction and leading hardware/software co-design across generations—helping build the computing foundation for the next decade of AI and accelerated computing.

What you'll be doing:

•
Design, implement, validate, and ship performance-centric features and programming-model capabilities in the CUDA driver and runtime, writing maintainable, well-tested production C/C++.

•
Optimize critical execution paths—including kernel launch, synchronization, memory management & movement, CPU–GPU coordination, and system interconnect use—for latency, throughput, bandwidth, efficiency, and scalability.

•
Own complex performance problems end-to-end - understand important workloads, form hypotheses, create focused measurements and models, isolate root causes across software and hardware boundaries, implement production solutions, and validate application-level impact.

•
Establish performance expectations for current and future platforms, characterize new silicon, close software and hardware gaps, and drive performance readiness through product release.

•
Translate workload and platform evidence into CUDA API and programming-model improvements, systems-software direction, and measurement-backed recommendations for future hardware architecture and implementation.

•
Partner with application, library, framework, operating-system, driver, runtime, firmware, GPU architecture, silicon, product, and customer-facing teams; communicate findings clearly and raise engineering quality through design and code reviews.

•
Lead complex feature development and cross-layer investigations across teams, define performance requirements and technical direction for major subsystems, mentor engineers, and shape hardware/software decisions for future product generations.

What we need to see:

•
A BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience — with at least 2 years of relevant systems-software development experience.

•
Strong production C/C++ systems-programming experience, including delivery of substantial features, optimizations, or production fixes in a complex codebase.

•
Strong operating systems and concurrency foundations, including threads, synchronization, processes, virtual memory, and user/kernel interactions.

•
Strong computer-architecture foundations, including processors, memory hierarchy, caching and coherence, data movement, and system interconnects.

•
Demonstrated success improving real software performance: measuring behavior, identifying the limiting mechanism, implementing an effective solution, and validating the result quantitatively.

•
Sound technical judgment, ownership of ambiguous problems, and clear communication across organizational and disciplinary boundaries.

•
Direct CUDA or GPU experience is valuable but is not required when accompanied by deep systems-software, operating-systems, computer-architecture, and performance-engineering foundations.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

•
Experience developing GPU or accelerator drivers, runtimes, kernel software, firmware, compilers, or other performance-critical low-level systems.

•
Experience with pre-silicon analysis, platform bring-up, performance modeling, or hardware/software co-design.

•
Systems-level performance experience with AI/DL, HPC, graphics, automotive, robotics, or similarly demanding workloads.

•
Evidence of technical invention(s), such as software-performance patents, novel production designs, or measurement-backed recommendations that influenced a hardware revision or future architecture.

•
Python or another scripting language used for focused experimentation, data analysis, or visualization.

NVIDIA is seeking a senior product leader to define the strategy and build the platforms that deliver high-quality training data for our foundation models. Starting with web and code data for Nemotron, you will help research teams discover valuable new sources from the open web, improve data quality and diversity, and turn raw content into datasets that advance model capabilities. In this founding product leadership role, you will partner with an engineering lead and work across research, data acquisition, data platforms, and legal teams to build the roadmap and investment priorities. You will connect data acquisition and curation decisions to measurable training outcomes, balancing quality, scale, delivery time, and cost. As research needs evolve, you will extend the platform to additional domains and modalities!

This role offers the opportunity to shape a foundational capability for NVIDIA’s AI models, working directly with researchers and engineers to improve what our models can learn. If you bring deep technical curiosity, product judgment, and a record of delivering ambitious data platforms, we want to hear from you.

What you’ll be doing:
